new.text: Changes to the reporting basis Three changes affect the comparison of the figures in this edition with those published for earlier years. They are summarised here and referred to where they apply in the later chapters. From this edition, leakage and energy figures are reported for the financial year from April to March instead of the calendar year, so that they can be compared directly with the regulatory returns. Figures for earlier years in this report have been restated on the same basis, and the restated values differ from those published previously by less than two per cent. The boundary of the Riverside zone was also redrawn in October to include the new housing at the former brickworks site. Zone-level comparisons with earlier years therefore use the old boundary, while network totals include all properties supplied at the end of the year. Finally, energy intensity is now calculated on the volume of water put into supply rather than the volume abstracted. The new definition matches the industry benchmark and removes the effect of process losses at the treatment works, which varied between sites and from year to year. 1.4

new.text: 2 Personal protective equipment Crews must wear the equipment listed below whenever they are on site, including during short visits to a valve chamber or a meter pit. • High-visibility jacket or vest, class 2 or above • Safety boots with steel toe caps and midsole protection • Hard hat when working near open excavations or overhead loads • Gloves suitable for the task: chemical gloves for chlorination work • Hearing protection at pumping stations and when using breakers • Full-body harness and lanyard for any work at height above two metres Inspect harnesses and lanyards before each use. Withdraw any harness with cut, burnt or stretched webbing and report it to the stores team the same day. Replacement equipment is issued by the depot stores on presentation of the damaged item. Lost items are replaced once per year without charge. 5A Lone working Lone working is allowed only for tasks listed as low risk in the job planning system, such as meter readings, valve exercising in footways and visual inspections of reservoirs from the outside. Before starting, the lone worker books the task in the check-in app and sets a check-in interval of no more than sixty minutes. If a check-in is missed, the control room calls the worker twice and then sends the nearest crew. • Carry a charged phone and the personal alarm issued by the depot. • Do not lift covers heavier than 25 kg without a second person. • Stop work and leave the site if a member of the public becomes aggressive. Confined spaces, work at height and work in live traffic lanes are never lone working tasks.
